title: Construction of isoscattering non-isospectral quantum graphs using the concept of a germ graph
authors: Omer Farooq, Michał Ławniczak, Leszek Sirko
abstract: The recently developed concept of germ graphs (P. Kurasov {\it et al.}, Phys. Rev. Research {\bf 7}, L022071 (2025)) is employed to construct families of isocattering, non-isospectral graphs that exhibit dissipation. More specifically, a new pair of isoscattering non-isospectral graphs is constructed by connecting the existing isoscattering non-isospectral graphs, so called attachments, to the different contact vertices of the germ graph. The existing isoscattering non-isospectral graphs contained a two-loop graph labelled $Γ_{A2}$ and a three-loop graph labelled $Γ_{A3}$. These graphs have an equal total metric length, but different topologies. The resulting graphs $Γ_3$ and $Γ_4$ are verified as non-isospectral using their Euler characteristics, while their isoscattering properties are investigated by calculating the one-port scattering matrices numerically.
summary: This paper utilizes the concept of germ graphs to construct two quantum graphs ($\Gamma_3$ and $\Gamma_4$) that serve as a counterexample in inverse scattering theory. The graphs are proven to be non-isospectral because their Euler characteristics differ, yet they are found to be isoscattering because their calculated one-port scattering matrices coincide numerically. This highlights that spectral and scattering information alone is insufficient to uniquely determine the structure of a quantum graph.
main_problem: The study addresses the non-uniqueness of reconstructing a physical system's structure from its spectral or scattering data.
main_result: The authors constructed a pair of quantum graphs ($\Gamma_3$ and $\Gamma_4$) that are non-isospectral (different Euler characteristics) yet exhibit identical one-port scattering matrices (isoscattering).
method: The analysis involves calculating the Euler characteristic ($\chi$) for spectral comparison and numerically computing the one-port scattering matrix ($S(\kappa)$) using directed-bond representations for scattering comparison.
model_or_system: The physical system is modeled by quantum graphs, specifically constructing extended graphs ($\Gamma_3, \Gamma_4$) by attaching smaller graphs ($\Gamma_{A2}, \Gamma_{A3}$) to a central 'germ graph' ($\Gamma_1$).
key_observables: Euler characteristic ($\chi$), one-port scattering matrix ($S(\kappa)$), modulus ($|S|$), and phase ($\varphi$) of the scattering matrix.
important_parameters: Total metric length ($L = 3.5 	ext{ m}$) and dissipation ($ eta = 0.0090 	ext{ m}^{-1/2}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Euler characteristic is a spectral invariant for the compact graphs considered.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the graph constructions ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_{A2}, \Gamma_{A3}$), and subsequent figures show the calculated modulus and phase of the scattering matrix for $\Gamma_3$ and $\Gamma_4$, demonstrating their numerical coincidence.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon the germ graph concept to construct extended graphs. It first establishes the properties of the attachment graphs ($\Gamma_{A2}, \Gamma_{A3}$) and then analyzes the resulting extended graphs ($\Gamma_3, \Gamma_4$) by comparing their topological invariants ($\chi$) and their scattering responses ($S(\kappa)$).
why_interesting: The demonstration of isoscattering, non-isospectral graphs provides a concrete example of spectral/scattering non-uniqueness, which is a fundamental concept in inverse scattering theory relevant to quantum systems.
